Work with the documents a run wrote.

A run report is the source of truth for everything go-mutants says: the console
summary, the exit status, and every later rendering are derived from it. These
subcommands read those documents rather than producing new measurements.

`list`, `latest` and `clean` work on the history go-mutants keeps for itself in
the operating system's cache directory, one document per run. `merge` and
`validate` work on files you name.

Usage:
  go-mutants report [flags]
  go-mutants report [command]

Available Commands:
  clean       Delete this module's run history
  latest      Print the newest run this module recorded, and where it is filed
  list        List the runs this module has recorded, newest first
  merge       Combine the reports of a sharded run into the whole run's report
  validate    Check a run report against the schema go-mutants publishes

Flags:
  -h, --help   help for report

Use "go-mutants report [command] --help" for more information about a command.

Exit codes:
  0    the run completed and no policy gate failed
  1    an opt-in gate failed (--strict, policy.minimum_score, init --check)
  2    an infrastructure, configuration, baseline, or expectation failure
  130  interrupted (Ctrl-C)
  143  terminated (SIGTERM)
